stories.title: Fortune 500 Company Signs Sugar Land Office Lease
stories.excerpt: Primoris Services, a Fortune 500 provider of critical infrastructure services Sugar has signed a 25,352-square-foot office lease at Sugar Land Town Square. The announcement comes as Sugar Land Town Square undergoes a significant redevelopment initiative designed to elevate the tenant experience and further strengthen the district’s appeal to corporate employers, supporting continued economic growth in Sugar Land and the Greater Houston region. Primoris will occupy the 8th floor of 2150 Town Square Place and is expected to begin occupancy in 2027. Primoris was self-represented in lease negotiations, while the landlord was represented by CBRE’s Bubba Harkins, Jenny Sealy and Joel Douthit. Primoris is a provider of infrastructure services to the utility, energy and renewables markets, offering engineering, construction and maintenance services across the utility, energy and renewable infrastructure sectors. Primoris joins a diverse roster of office tenants, including CVR Energy, Industrial Info Resources and Nexus Water Group. In 2025, the City of Sugar Land approved a $12.5 million reinvestment in Sugar Land Town Square to enhance the property and further elevate the tenant experience. The post Fortune 500 Company Signs Sugar Land Office Lease appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Primoris (Fortune 500 infrastructure) leases 25,352 SF at Sugar Land Town Square, occupancy 2027.
Sugar Land City approved $12.5M reinvestment in Town Square to attract corporate tenants.
Lease signals Houston-area office recovery; mixed-use redevelopment designed for employer appeal.
stories.summary: Primoris Services, a Fortune 500 critical infrastructure provider, has signed a 25,352-square-foot office lease on the 8th floor of 2150 Town Square Place in Sugar Land with occupancy expected in 2027. The announcement coincides with the City of Sugar Land's $12.5 million reinvestment initiative in Sugar Land Town Square, part of a larger redevelopment designed to elevate tenant experience and strengthen appeal to corporate employers. The property also houses CVR Energy, Industrial Info Resources, and Nexus Water Group, indicating a diversified tenant base anchoring the mixed-use office district.
stories.impact: Primoris's commitment signals growing corporate office demand in Sugar Land and the greater Houston region, validating mixed-use redevelopment strategy that competes with downtown Houston. This office anchor may accelerate adjacent multifamily absorption in Sugar Land's core—developers should monitor residential pipeline, walkability amenities, and capture rates on new class-A apartment starts near Town Square over the next 18–24 months as employment density increases.

stories.title: HBK CPAs & Consultants Relocates Baltimore Offices to Hunt Valley Complex
stories.excerpt: HBK CPAs & Consultants has signed a lease with Hill Management Services, Inc. for 7,168 square feet of space and recently relocated its Baltimore regional office, together with 15 employees, to the Executive Plaza complex in Hunt Valley, Maryland. Danielle Bridge of Hill Management Services represented the landlord, and Clare Berrang of Singer Demareck Real Estate handled negotiations on behalf of the tenant. The Youngstown, Ohio-based accounting firm entered the Baltimore market following the company’s acquisition of the 30-person McLean, Koehler, Sparks & Hammond late last year.Located at 11350 McCormick Road, the business complex consists of four office towers comprising 550,000 square feet of commercial office space. “Executive Plaza’s positioning within a robust and diverse business community, which provides the perfect environment to service existing customers as well as opportunities to generate new clients, makes the complex ideal for professional services firms such as HBK,” said Beyrodt. The post HBK CPAs & Consultants Relocates Baltimore Offices to Hunt Valley Complex appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: HBK CPAs & Consultants relocates Baltimore regional office (15 employees) to Hunt Valley.
Lease follows HBK's 2024 acquisition of McLean, Koehler, Sparks & Hammond (30-person firm).
Hunt Valley complex offers 550,000 SF across four office towers in established business district.
stories.summary: HBK CPAs & Consultants, a Youngstown, Ohio-based accounting firm, has signed a 7,168-square-foot lease with Hill Management Services for space in the Executive Plaza complex (11350 McCormick Road) in Hunt Valley, Maryland, and relocated its Baltimore regional office with 15 employees to the location. The move follows HBK's acquisition last year of McLean, Koehler, Sparks & Hammond, a 30-person Baltimore-area firm. The 550,000-square-foot Executive Plaza comprises four office towers in Hunt Valley's established business community.
stories.impact: While primarily an office transaction, HBK's consolidation and regional growth in Baltimore's Hunt Valley submarket suggests professional services employment is stabilizing there. This modest office activity has minimal direct bearing on multifamily demand; however, it reinforces Hunt Valley as a secondary employment node that may support steady-state apartment demand rather than growth—developers should focus multifamily efforts on higher-velocity job centers (Inner Harbor, Towson) rather than office-dependent Hunt Valley.

stories.title: Breakthrough Properties Acquires, Fully Leases Puget Sound Biomanufacturing Campus
stories.excerpt: Breakthrough Properties, a joint venture between Tishman Speyer and Bellco Capital, has acquired a recently delivered biomanufacturing facility at 215 Shuksan Way in Everett, Washington, just outside of Seattle. The joint venture acquired the 270,000-square-foot property for $78 million from its second life science fund. In tandem with the acquisition, Breakthrough secured a separate 21-year lease for the entire campus with a global biopharma company to create a U.S. manufacturing facility. 215 Shuksan Way offers a full range of capabilities and amenities, from drug manufacturing, quality control labs and warehouse and distribution logistics to administrative office spaces. The acquisition marks Breakthrough’s first investment in the Puget Sound region. 215 Shuksan Way sits approximately 25 miles north of Seattle along the I-5 corridor. The location provides easy connectivity to Seattle-Tacoma International Airport, the commercial airport Paine Field, the Port of Everett and railway access that connects the site to major North American freight corridors. Concurrently, the JV secured a separate 21-year lease with a global biopharma company to operate a U.S. manufacturing facility at the site. The property, located approximately 25 miles north of Seattle along the I-5 corridor, offers drug manufacturing, quality control labs, warehouse/distribution, and administrative office space, with convenient access to SeaTac International, Paine Field, Port of Everett, and rail infrastructure.
stories.impact: Large biopharma manufacturing commitment to Everett signals supply-chain resilience and potential for sustained high-skill employment growth north of Seattle. Developers should anticipate downstream demand for workforce housing (both market-rate and potentially employer-subsidized) in Everett and Snohomish County submarkets. The 21-year lease duration indicates stable, long-term employer presence—favorable signal for multifamily absorption and rent growth in proximity to I-5 and industrial corridors serving the facility.

stories.title: J.G. Petrucci, BGO Cold Chain Lease Bethlehem Cold Storage Development
stories.excerpt: J.G. Petrucci Company, Inc. and BGO Cold Chain announced that Freshpet has leased the entire 216,000-square-foot cold storage development at 757 Hellertown Road in Bethlehem, Pennsylvania. The facility is scheduled for on-time and on-budget completion by the end of the year, and the property was developed through a joint venture between Petrucci and BGO Cold Chain. The facility is Freshpet’s first dedicated cold storage facility, contributing to the effective distribution of its temperature-sensitive products. The location offers excellent proximity to the company’s existing Bethlehem Kitchen and convenient access to I-78 and other major roadways. Freshpet’s commercial office is in Bedminster, New Jersey, and it has additional Kitchens in Ennis, Texas.Construction was completed by Petrucci’s in-house construction management firm, Iron Hill Construction Management. “Freshpet’s lease of the entire facility underscores the growing demand for modern cold chain infrastructure in this market,” said Kevin Rivest, Managing Partner, BGO. stories.impact: Freshpet's capital commitment to cold-chain logistics in Bethlehem signals supply-chain optimization and potential for facility expansion or workforce hiring in the Lehigh Valley. stories.title: Historic Trinity Lutheran Church in Everett Listed for Sale
stories.excerpt: Trinity Lutheran Church in Everett, Washington, has listed its historic property at 2324 Lombard Avenue for sale. Kidder Mathews Senior Vice President Steve Pelluer and Associate Vice President Zeke Pelluer are representing the congregation. For more than a century, Trinity has been a place of worship, inclusion, and service. Organized in 1904 as St. Paul Lutheran Church, it became Trinity English Lutheran Church in 1914. “Properties with this combination of character, history, flexibility, and community significance rarely become available,” said Steve Pelluer. Designed by Seattle architecture firm Bebb and Gould, the historic sanctuary has served as a worship site for generations. The 13,728-square-foot property includes 9,644 square feet of church space and a 4,084-square-foot administration building. The 0.41-acre property is adjacent to Clark Park and near downtown Everett, Everett High School, and North Middle School. The church portion dates to the early 1920s, with additions completed in 1940 and 1969. The post Historic Trinity Lutheran Church in Everett Listed for Sale appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Historic Trinity Lutheran Church (1904–present) lists 13,728 SF property, Everett, WA for sale.
0.41-acre site: 9,644 SF church, 4,084 SF administration building; adjacent Clark Park.
Location: near downtown Everett, Everett High School, North Middle School; designed by Bebb & Gould.
stories.summary: Trinity Lutheran Church in Everett, Washington, has listed its historic property at 2324 Lombard Avenue for sale. The 13,728-square-foot parcel (0.41 acres) includes 9,644 square feet of church space and a 4,084-square-foot administration building, designed by Seattle architecture firm Bebb and Gould. The property, originally organized in 1904, is located adjacent to Clark Park and near downtown Everett, Everett High School, and North Middle School. Kidder Mathews is representing the congregation.
stories.impact: Historic church property sale in downtown Everett signals potential land-use conversion opportunity; the 0.41-acre site with mixed church/office infrastructure near parks and schools is a plausible adaptive-reuse or redevelopment candidate for workforce housing or mixed-use infill. Developers should monitor sale outcome; if acquired by a developer, this small-format site could pioneer downtown Everett residential infill aligned with biomanufacturing employment demand flagged in Article 3.

stories.title: Nalcorp, Clipper Equity Buy Coney Island Oceanfront Development Site for $20M
stories.excerpt: Fancy a trip to the Boardwalk? A pair of New York-based real estate development and investment firms — Nalcorp and Clipper Equity — have acquired a land parcel at 2015 Boardwalk West, an oceanfront development in Coney Island, Brooklyn, from seller Bath Site LLC for $20 million, broker TerraCRG announced Friday. The parking lot property, which spans 69,530 square feet and has 247 feet of Boardwalk frontage, seems to be part of a larger ongoing development on the site. Permits were filed in 2024 to build a 23-story, 202-unit mixed-use building at 2015 Boardwalk West. The larger parcel of land home to the development was purchased in 2006 by the City Investment Fund — a real estate private equity vehicle launched by the Fisher Brothers and Morgan Stanley — from Thor Equities for $90 million. Following the 2006 sale, the larger parcel was subdivided into six separate tax lots, including the one part of this most recent transaction, which is called Block 7072, Lot 6. Bath Site LLC — an entity comprising Georgica Green Ventures and its nonprofit partner RiseBoro Community Partnership — acquired this property in July 2024 for $10.4 million. Dan Marks and Daniel Lebor from TerraCRG represented Bath Site LLC in this transaction. The firm did not disclose the names of the brokers who represented the buyers. The buyers did not immediately respond to Commercial Observer’s request for comment, while the seller could not be reached for comment. “Coney Island has become one of New York City’s most exciting waterfront growth stories,” Marks said in a statement. “Ongoing public and private investment has transformed the area into one of the city’s most compelling waterfront markets. Developers should monitor permitting velocity and construction start timing—Coney Island's limited oceanfront supply and stabilizing NYC multifamily market make this a high-profile delivery candidate. Adjacent and competing projects in South Brooklyn should anticipate leasing pressure and rent-growth moderation when 23-story delivery arrives.

stories.title: Survey: 61% of Investors Hold Negative Multifamily Outlook in 2026, Per Berkadia
stories.excerpt: Housing isn’t making anyone happy these days. In a survey of more than 100 principals and executives across private real estate investment firms, Berkadia found that 61 percent of respondents characterized their outlook for the multifamily market in the second half of 2026 as negative due to capital markets volatility, Commercial Observer can first report. Meanwhile, 52 percent said that the asset class performed worse in the first half of the year than they had anticipated. “Six months ago, investors were very optimistic that [volatility] was going to fade and transaction activity was going to accelerate,” said Josh Bodin, senior vice president of capital markets strategy and trading at Berkadia, in a conversation with CO. “Instead, the operating environment has remained a lot more uncertain, interest rate volatility has persisted and property performance has stayed softer than expected,” he added. Bond yields have been high for most of 2026. The 10-Year Treasury currently sits at 4.7 percent, its highest levels since 2023, while the 30-Year Treasury sits at 5.2 percent, a 20-year high. In a separate report, CBRE found that first-quarter investment sales in multifamily hit $29.5 billion, a 6 percent decline year-over-year, while the second quarter saw a rebound of investment sales activity to $34.9 billion (that total was still down by 2.7 percent year-over-year). However, Bodin emphasized these metrics and investors’ sentiments haven’t translated into a loss of confidence in multifamily as an asset class, but has instead changed how investors view execution risk. To this end, Berkadia’s survey found that 82 percent of investors plan to expand their portfolios in the coming months and that 83 percent expect market conditions to improve by late 2027. “On the tailwinds side, near-term, supply deliveries are beginning to moderate in many markets, capital remains really available for well-positioned assets and investors increasingly expect conditions to improve,” said
bullets: Berkadia survey: 61% of multifamily investors hold negative 2026 H2 outlook (100+ principals polled).
52% reported asset class performance worse than expected in H1 2026.
Key concerns: capital markets volatility, persistent interest-rate uncertainty, softer-than-expected property performance.
stories.summary: A Berkadia survey of over 100 principals and executives across private real estate investment firms found that 61 percent characterized their multifamily outlook for the second half of 2026 as negative due to capital markets volatility, interest-rate uncertainty, and softer operating performance. Additionally, 52 percent said the asset class performed worse in the first half of 2026 than anticipated. Josh Bodin, senior vice president of capital markets strategy at Berkadia, noted that six months ago investors expected volatility to fade and transaction activity to accelerate, but instead the operating environment has remained uncertain, with the 10-Year Treasury at 4.7 percent and the 30-Year at 5.2 percent.
stories.impact: Sustained investor pessimism on multifamily signals constrained capital availability, higher cost of debt, and depressed acquisitions pricing power for 2026—critical for developers' refinancing and bridge financing strategies. Elevated long-dated rates (10Y at 4.7%, 30Y at 5.2%) push underwriting yields higher and compress development IRRs, making only best-in-class locations and strong sponsor balance sheets competitive for financing. Expect continued selective deal flow, higher debt service coverage requirements, and opportunity for well-capitalized developers to acquire distressed assets or repositioned properties at valley pricing.

stories.title: St. Regis Bal Harbour Resort Secures $263M Refi After Special Servicing
stories.excerpt: Fortress Investment Group has rescued Al Rayyan Tourism Investment Company (ARTIC)’s St. Regis Bal Harbour Resort out of special servicing, supplying a $263 million loan to refinance the oceanfront property. The New York-based lender assumed $188 million in existing debt and added $70 million in new debt backing the 213-room property in Bal Harbour, Fla., north of Miami Beach, according to public mortgage documents, which valued the asset at $311 million. The new financing comes nearly a year after a $188 million commercial mortgage-backed securities (CMBS) loan tied to the resort headed to special servicing as the financing was set to mature. Although the loan remained current and the resort maintained a debt service coverage ratio above break-even, its cash flow in 2024 was about half of 2021 levels, the year it had secured the debt. The lender, Column Financial, wanted ARTIC to buy a replacement interest rate cap, which it had yet to secure, Morningstar reported. ARTIC, which is run by a member of the Qatari ruling family, had purchased the resort for $213 million in 2014, three years after it was completed. The complex, which features three 27-story towers at 9703 Collins Avenue, houses two pools, a 14,000-square-foot spa, five dining outposts, 13,000 square feet of event space as well as a condo component. The hotel owner and condo owners have sparred. In 2024, the condo association sued ARTIC over alleged building defects, safety hazards, and financial mismanagement. The parties settled the suit a year later. Fortress Investment Group and ARTIC did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Fortress Investment Group refinances St. Regis Bal Harbour Resort out of special servicing; $263M loan.
Asset valued at $311M; assumed $188M existing debt, added $70M new debt for 213-room property.
Prior loan ($188M CMBS, Column Financial) headed to special servicing; 2024 cash flow ~50% of 2021.
stories.summary: Fortress Investment Group has provided a $263 million refinancing loan to rescue Al Rayyan Tourism Investment Company's St. Regis Bal Harbour Resort from special servicing. The loan assumed $188 million in existing debt and added $70 million in new debt, with the property valued at $311 million. The prior $188 million CMBS loan, originated by Column Financial, had headed to special servicing as it matured; although the loan remained current and the resort maintained positive debt service coverage, its 2024 cash flow was approximately half of 2021 levels, and the lender required replacement interest-rate cap coverage.
stories.impact: Hospitality distress (even for luxury oceanfront assets) reflects travel and event volatility; minimal direct impact on multifamily development. However, the rescue indicates Fortress's appetite for hospitality-focused distressed debt, signaling that hotel refinancings remain fragile and may compete for capital with multifamily bridge and mezzanine opportunities. Developers should monitor whether rate volatility and rising long-dated yields continue to pressure hospitality and mixed-use projects, potentially freeing capital for pure-play multifamily.

stories.title: First Pioneer Properties Buys Queens Retail Center for $24M
stories.excerpt: New York-based real estate management and development firm First Pioneer Properties, along with ABS Partners Real Estate, has acquired a Queens retail center from Levy Properties for $23.5 million, property records made public Thursday show. The one-story property at 213-04 Northern Boulevard in Bayside is currently home to an urgent care medical office and Bebeang Baby Store. Jennifer Markowitz of Levy Properties signed the deal for the seller, while Suresh Sani, owner of First Pioneer Properties, signed for the buyers. ABS seems to act as a frequent co-investor and partner of First Pioneer Properties. It’s unclear who brokered the deal. The buyers and seller did not immediately respond to Commercial Observer’s requests for comment. The property has 24,000 square feet of built space and 74,350 square feet of additional air rights for a total of 98,478 buildable square feet, according to data from PincusCo. The buyers’ intentions for the property are unclear, but Queens has been awash with multifamily developments lately. This month, Wells Fargo provided a $175 million construction loan to the Domain Companies for a 429-unit mixed-income housing development at 35-45, 35-33 and 35-42 41st Street in Astoria. Also this month, LMXD and BedRock Real Estate Partners closed on a $250 million loan to build a housing development at 35-10 Steinway Street in Astoria. Earlier this summer, another Queens retail property changed hands when Punia & Marx Real Estate sold the Whitestone Shopping Center at 153-15 Cross Island Parkway for $56 million. Meanwhile, a historic Queens bowling alley — Whitestone Lanes — at 30-05 Whitestone Expressway in Flushing — sold for $45 million in June as part of a major multifamily development project coming to the area. Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: First Pioneer Properties & ABS Partners acquire Queens retail center (Bayside) for $23.5M.
24,000 SF built space + 74,350 SF air rights (total 98,478 SF buildable); urgent care + retail tenants.
Article notes Queens multifamily development surge; buyers' intentions for property unclear.
stories.summary: First Pioneer Properties and ABS Partners Real Estate have acquired a one-story retail center at 213-04 Northern Boulevard in Bayside, Queens, for $23.5 million from Levy Properties. The property comprises 24,000 square feet of built space and 74,350 square feet of additional air rights (total 98,478 buildable square feet) and currently houses an urgent care medical office and Bebeang Baby Store. The buyers' intentions are unclear, though Queens has been experiencing strong multifamily development activity and the air-rights component suggests potential for vertical expansion.
stories.impact: Queens retail-to-residential conversion opportunity: First Pioneer's acquisition of a one-story medical/retail center with substantial air rights in Bayside—a transit-accessible, family-oriented Flushing submarket—signals likely multifamily redevelopment. Developers should monitor air-rights assemblage and entitlement velocity; Bayside's supply constraints, proximity to transportation, and service demand create favorable conditions for workforce housing (2–3 BR units) or family-oriented multifamily. Article's reference to Queens multifamily surge suggests competitive market—early entitlement and acquisition may drive timing advantage.

stories.title: Pinnacle Group Offloads $128M Condominium and Commercial Portfolio in NYC
stories.excerpt: Pinnacle Group has offloaded a $128 million residential and retail condominium portfolio in New York City, less than a year after selling off its rent-stabilized assets. The massive trade, filed in city records this week, spanned 39 transactions across Queens, Brooklyn and Manhattan. It included nearly 750 residential units, as well as dozens of retail condominiums and several parking lots. The Real Deal first reported on the sale. The buyer entities, Friar Park JW, share an address with law firm Kurzman Eisenberg Corbin & Lever. The transactions were signed by Stuart Berg, chair of the firm’s real estate practice group. A PincusCo report tied the Friar Park entities and Berg to Tremada Holdings, an affiliate of London-based property company William Pears Group. The group, through Tremada, has quietly executed bulk residential transactions across New York City over the years with Berg’s law firm, according to PincusCo. Berg, as well as spokespeople for William Pears Group and Tremada, did not respond to requests for comment. Queens-based property management company Bronstein Properties is the managing agent for the portfolio of units, according to a spokesperson for Bronstein. Pinnacle, led by Joel Wiener, made headlines in May 2025 when it placed a portfolio of roughly 5,000 rent-stabilized apartments across New York City into bankruptcy after facing approximately $574.4 million in debt. Summit Properties won the auction for the portfolio in January, paying $451.3 million for the units. The proceeds from Pinnacle’s most recent sale will pay $66 million to lender Axos Capital, TRD reported, citing filings with the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange by Pinnacle’s Israeli subsidiary Zarasai Group. Another $47 million is currently slated to be deposited into the account of Series C bondholders. A spokesperson for Pinnacle Group could not be reached for comment on the sales. Buyer entities (Friar Park JW) tied to William Pears Group (London-based); portfolio spans Queens, Brooklyn, Manhattan.

stories.summary: Pinnacle Group has offloaded a $128 million residential and retail condominium portfolio across New York City in a massive trade comprising 39 transactions. The portfolio spans Queens, Brooklyn, and Manhattan and includes nearly 750 residential units, dozens of retail condominiums, and several parking lots. Buyer entities Friar Park JW, tied to London-based William Pears Group (through affiliate Tremada Holdings), executed the trade less than a year after Pinnacle sold off its rent-stabilized assets. The transactions indicate a strategic exit by Pinnacle and acquisition activity by international institutional capital.
stories.impact: Portfolio sale signals NYC residential market consolidation and institutional buyer appetite for stabilized rental condo/mixed portfolios—favorable for aggregators and long-hold value plays, but may compress transaction pricing for smaller developers. William Pears Group's quiet bulk acquisition strategy in NYC suggests patient, international capital is accumulating assets; developers should anticipate competitive tension on portfolio acquisitions and stabilized asset prices. The scale and geography (Queens, Brooklyn, Manhattan) indicate strategic build toward scale operations, signaling that pure-play value-add multifamily is attractive to permanent capital at current risk-adjusted returns.
